name: pgvectorscale
tagline: TigerData's Postgres extension adding StreamingDiskANN indexes on top of pgvector.
description: pgvectorscale is an open-source PostgreSQL extension from TigerData (formerly Timescale) that complements pgvector with a StreamingDiskANN index, based on Microsoft's DiskANN research, plus Statistical Binary Quantization and label-based filtered search. Indexes are designed to live on SSD rather than RAM, giving high recall and throughput at a lower cost than in-memory HNSW for large tables. It keeps pgvector's vector type and query syntax, so adopting it is mostly a matter of creating a different index. It is PostgreSQL-licensed and preinstalled on Tiger Cloud.

pricing.notes: Free; included on TigerData's Tiger Cloud managed Postgres.

scale.notes: Single Postgres primary; SSD-resident DiskANN indexes handle tens to hundreds of millions of vectors per node.

strengths: DiskANN-style index keeps vectors on SSD instead of RAM
Statistical Binary Quantization improves accuracy over plain binary quantization
Label-based filtering integrated into the index
Drop-in on top of pgvector types and operators
weaknesses: Not available on most hyperscaler managed Postgres
Index builds are still slower than IVF-based approaches
Feature set narrower than dedicated vector databases
useCases: Large pgvector tables that no longer fit HNSW in RAM
notIdealFor: RDS/Cloud SQL users who cannot install extensions
Workloads needing BM25 hybrid ranking out of the box
